title: The last RETURN-only cleanup trap in the plugin, on the binary every hook fires: _pxt_ignfile is created at :5340 under TMPDIR and armed at :5341 with `trap 'rm -f "$_pxt_ignfile"' RETURN` -- RETURN only. bin/edm-state:54 is `set -euo pipefail`, so an errexit abort inside pattern_extract_titles (the three unguarded awk calls at :5349/:5360/:5382) exits the process without firing the function's RETURN trap, and an INT/TERM/HUP during awk does the same. _pxt_ignfile is `local` at :5339, so no process-wide EXIT trap could reference it either -- the exact scoping problem tiering-matrix.sh solved with "${tmp:-}". This is the ONLY RETURN trap left in the plugin besides the FIXED one at tiering-matrix.sh:158, whose own comment at :148 describes this defect verbatim ('RETURN-only leaked $tmp on a die (exit 2, no RETURN) or a SIGINT mid-self-test'). CA-014 identified the shape, CA-481(a) finished converting the other site, this one was never swept. Held at P2 because the path is `edm-state update-patterns`, not every hook fire. Fix: four-arm form with RETURN on the EXIT arm and "${_pxt_ignfile:-}" guards; check the :5554 call path for with_state_lock nesting first.

The CA-481(c) sweep landed but is structurally blind to two shapes it exists to catch. _ca481_sweep's awk (:9640-9664) derives the signal list as the text after the LAST quote character, so an unquoted handler (`trap cleanup EXIT`) yields sig="" and contributes nothing: not flagged by combined mode, and never registered in file_has_exit so no-hup mode cannot report the file either. Two live sites are in that form -- evals/run-eval.sh:276 and bin/tests/wave6-smoke.sh:37 -- and both pass only because their other three arms happen to be quoted. Decisive: the historical CA-482 regression at wave6-smoke.sh WAS the unquoted form (`:34`'s comment describes `trap cleanup_wave6 EXIT INT TERM HUP`), so re-introducing it today passes silently, while the same bug written with quotes is caught -- a one-character difference decides whether the tripwire fires. Second blind spot, same root cause: a RETURN-only trap yields sig=" RETURN", has_exit false, invisible -- which is exactly why L5-001 survived a green sweep that names bin/* in scope. Both positive controls (:9687, :9694) use the quoted form and never probe this boundary. Fix: parse the signal list positionally (strip `trap`, drop a quoted handler or exactly one bare token, parse the rest), add unquoted-combined and RETURN-only positive controls, and treat RETURN as EXIT-class for no-hup registration.

The last two scratch files in wave6-smoke.sh are rooted outside the suite's trap-covered root: :4929 and :4930 use mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/edm-ca059-{1,2}.XXXXXX" instead of ${TMP} (created :21, owned by the four-arm trap at :37-40), with a single tail rm -f at :4960 as their only cleanup. Every other mktemp site in the file interpolates ${TMP}. The interrupt window is real, not theoretical: :4932-4937 launches two background edm-state processes that deliberately contend for the same state lock and then waits on both, and :4945-4946 runs cat under `set -euo pipefail` (:6) before the tail removal, so an unexpected read failure aborts ahead of :4960. The consistent-project-pattern defence fails outright -- this same file states the nest-under-$TMP rule at :463-464 -- and this is the exact class just remediated across eleven sites in wave7-smoke.sh under CA-495(b). Fix: change both templates to "${TMP}/edm-ca059-{1,2}.XXXXXX" and keep :4960 as a fast path.

CA-171 upgraded from NOTED after three rounds: five untrapped temp files at :45, :63, :115, :139, :191, each with only a tail rm -f (:56, :94, :133, :180, :224) and NO trap coverage at all -- the file's first trap is at :265 and its body removes only $CA146_SCRATCH. The upgrade trigger is :64, `_ac2_sleep_fn() { pwd > "$_ac2_pathfile"; sleep 5; }`, polled by :73 for up to 100 iterations: a deliberate multi-second window, the widest signal-deliverable window anywhere in the test tree, with _ac2_pathfile unhandled across it. A Ctrl-C there leaks with near-certainty, not by unlucky timing. Round 10's holding rationale ('assertion helpers never exit early') is correct about the errexit path under :5's set -euo pipefail but says nothing about the signal path. Consistency argues for filing: CA-481(b) was filed and fixed over a ONE-STATEMENT window and CA-495(b) over subshells that did carry tail removals. Fix: one four-arm trap after :45 covering all five by name with ${var:-} guards, or mint a suite-level $TMP root with the canonical four-arm trap and nest all five inside it, keeping the tail rm -f's as a fast path.

--generate-fixture's self-minted 50-initiative tree is never removed on any path and never pruned across invocations. :243 is `: "${DIR:=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/edm-timing-fixture.XXXXXX")}"`, populated by the :247-251 loop into 50 state files plus 50 per-initiative .gitignore files. _timing_cleanup (:42-48) sweeps exactly TMP_PC/TMP_LG/TMP_SS/TMP_LINT/TMP_MR; DIR is excluded, and the exclusion rationale at :40-41 ('may be a caller-supplied --dir the caller expects to keep') covers only the caller-supplied case -- but `:=` means the mktemp fires ONLY when --dir was omitted, i.e. precisely the branch where the tree is minted by the script and owned by nobody. The rationale therefore documents the branch that creates nothing and not the branch that does. :252-253 prints the path for reuse with no removal instruction, so a developer iterating on latency work accumulates one 50-initiative tree per invocation indefinitely; on macOS the system temp directory is per-user and survives reboots. Held at P2 because timing.sh is explicitly not discovered by run-all.sh (:29-30) and never fires in CI. Fix: set a _TIMING_OWNS_DIR flag in the := branch and add DIR to _timing_cleanup's loop guarded on it, preserving the caller-supplied carve-out exactly.

The CA-148/CA-149 .gitignore coverage assertion pins only the .edm-state lockbase. All six entries at :6843-6849 derive from ${state_file%.json}; none covers the second live lockbase CA-382 generalized to (code-audit/findings-ledger, bin/edm-state:4479). Coverage itself DOES hold by construction -- the per-initiative *.lock and *.lockd* at bin/edm-state:2229-2230 carry no slash so gitignore matches at any depth, and root :35-36 use **/ -- so this is a missing assertion, not a live exposure. Latent asymmetry worth recording: root :30 is a PREFIX glob (**/.edm-state.lock*), which is what makes .edm-state.lock.timeout.<pid> match; for every other lockbase only the ends-in forms **/*.lock and **/*.lockd* exist, so a hypothetical findings-ledger.lock.timeout.<pid> matches nothing in either file. Not reachable today -- the live timeout marker is TMPDIR-based (bin/edm-state:1348, post-G17/CA-305) and the in-directory legacy shape predates the CA-382 lockbase generalization, so no version created it off a non-edm-state lockbase. Filed so a future round need not re-derive the reachability argument. Fix: add two findings-ledger-derived entries to the :6843 list using the source's own formula, and either widen both .gitignore writers to *.lock* or add a one-line note at bin/edm-state:2229.

CA-495 CONFIRMED FIXED, both halves. (a) :8224 is now tmp_g22b="$(mktemp -d "${TMP}/edm-g22b.XXXXXX")", matching its G22a sibling at :8193, with :8223's `trap - EXIT INT TERM HUP` untouched exactly as the round-10 fix instruction prescribed, so the parent trap at :27-30 reclaims it on every path. (b) A whole-file grep for `mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}` in wave7-smoke.sh now returns exactly one hit, :24, the suite root itself -- all eleven conditional-leak siblings are converted to ${TMP}.

CA-481(a) CONFIRMED FIXED. :158-161 is the canonical four-arm split -- `trap 'rm -f "${tmp:-}"' RETURN EXIT`, INT/exit 130, TERM/exit 143, HUP/exit 129 -- with RETURN correctly sharing EXIT's cleanup-only body and the rationale recorded at :154-157. The last HUP-omitting and last cleanup-then-resume trap in evals/ is gone.

CA-481(b) CONFIRMED FIXED. :766-769 arms a first-stage four-arm trap covering $_CMP_TA alone immediately after the :758 mktemp, superseded by the two-file four-arm trap at :771-774 after :770's second mktemp. The one-statement untrapped window is closed, matching the bin/edm-lint-artifacts:143/:153-156 reference form.

CA-481(c) CONFIRMED LANDED after failing to land across three rounds. :9624-9699 scans bin/*, bin/tests/*.sh and evals/*.sh in two modes -- `combined` (no single trap statement may pair EXIT with a real signal) and `no-hup` (every file installing an EXIT cleanup trap must also install a HUP trap) -- with two planted positive controls at :9686 and :9693 proving neither check passes vacuously. This gives positive assurance for every file whose EXIT trap uses a quoted handler; the residual gaps are filed as L5-002 and are precisely why L5-001 survived.

CA-480 re-verified as NOT an L5 finding. On L5's own axis the orphan is harmless: both .lockd and its .stale.$$ aside are matched by root .gitignore:36 (**/*.lockd*) and by the per-initiative file (bin/edm-state:2230, bin/edm-init:180), so a bricked lockdir never surfaces in git status. Its impact is availability (L3), not hygiene. Recorded only so the round does not double-count it.

CA-169 confirmed intact and must stay unapplied: with_state_lock deliberately never unlinks the flock lockfile because mutual exclusion is keyed on the inode, and both entry points write .edm-state.lock* into the per-initiative .gitignore. Now machine-pinned -- bin/tests/wave7-smoke.sh:5876-5889 locates the `# CA-169:` marker by content rather than line number and asserts it sits immediately above the real flock() call, failing loudly on a stale anchor. The two narrow documented exceptions (bin/edm-state:3339, :3777) are themselves pinned at wave7-smoke.sh:8526. Do not fix in a later round.

Flock timeout marker verified clean, no finding: ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/edm-state.lock-timeout.${BASHPID:-$$} -- never in a tracked directory, pre-cleared at :1349, mkdir only on the timeout branch at :1351, removed at :1365. The ${BASHPID:-$$} form also removes the subshell-PID-collision hazard a bare $$ would carry. Its shared-/tmp predictable-name exposure is an L8 axis already tracked under CA-305/CA-347.

write_atomic's staging files verified fully ignore-covered across all four live call sites: :2176 (state file -> .edm-state.json.tmp.*), :4462 (findings-ledger.md -> **/*.md.tmp.* and per-initiative *.md.tmp.*), :5554 (docs/audit-patterns/*.md -> root .gitignore:16 and :37), :6200 (HANDOFF.md -> *.md.tmp.*). Re-confirmed that NO .jsonl destination passes through write_atomic -- findings-ledger.jsonl is written by the synthesizer's Write tool -- so the absent *.jsonl.tmp.* pattern stays unreachable. Two of these shapes are asserted at bin/tests/wave7-smoke.sh:6846-6847.

The per-initiative .gitignore is byte-identical across both entry points (bin/edm-state:2225-2232 and bin/edm-init:175-182, six lines each), and bin/edm-init:187-188 conditionally appends .edm-state.json under commit_state_file=false so it travels with a relocated srd_root rather than living in a second disconnected file. bin/edm-state:2220-2222 records why the duplicate write is harmless (cat > overwrites, never appends). CA-213/CA-314/CA-341 all confirmed fixed here.

evals/runs/ verified self-ignoring (`*` plus `!.gitignore`) so run output can never surface as untracked, with retention enforced by prune_old_runs reached from all four exit paths via cleanup() and the CLEANUP_DONE latch at run-eval.sh:255-259. CA-066, CA-188, CA-214, CA-291, CA-292 and CA-443 all confirmed fixed here.

--out DIR pointed at an unignored in-repo directory would deposit untracked run output, but this is deliberate and documented, and pruning of a caller-chosen root requires an explicit EDM_EVAL_PRUNE_EXPLICIT_OUT=true opt-in precisely because that root may hold content the driver does not own. Operator choice, not a defect.

bin/edm-check-grants, bin/edm-lint-artifacts and bin/edm-sync-canonical-sections all verified canonical: edm-lint-artifacts:143 + :153-156 then :163 + :168-171 is the reference two-stage four-arm form the CA-481(b) fix was modelled on; edm-check-grants:123 + :131-134 arms four-arm on the line after its mktemp; edm-sync-canonical-sections:81-86 has the CA-519 writability-guard hoist above the mktemp and a staging path double-covered by root .gitignore:37 and :40.

_harness.sh's two scratch helpers are correct by construction: :75 + :88-91 (harness_scratch_dir) and :107 + :122-125 (with_scratch_repo), the latter with full trap -p save/restore at :114-117 and :154-158. Both root at ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} legitimately -- they ARE the scratch root, not something nested inside one. :76-79 records the CA-159 rule that a path is never interpolated into a trap body string.

The hundreds of *.tmp-plus-mv pairs across wave6-smoke.sh all write inside the suite's own $TMP tree, which the four-arm trap at :37-40 owns. Correct by construction. CA-030/CA-045/CA-216 confirmed fixed -- the T41 tracked-file backup/restore is inside cleanup_wave6.

harness-smoke.sh's CA-146 scratch tree IS correctly trapped: :263 + :265-268 four-arm, with the nested per-case subdirectories at :283-386 all inside it and :397 clearing dispositions at the end. Recorded separately from L5-004 so the two are not conflated -- L5-004 concerns the five OTHER files in that file, created before any trap exists.

hooks.json creates no runtime files of its own -- every hook body delegates to a bin/ helper whose temp handling is audited above. No .pid, no lock, no log, no cache, no SQLite anywhere in the file. Nothing to report on this lens.

Whole-plugin negative sweep: no PID file, log file, SQLite database, cache directory, __pycache__, dist/, build/, downloaded artifact or generated-secret surface exists anywhere in the plugin. The only pidfile-shaped construct is with_state_lock's lockdir sentinel at :1476-1483, which lives INSIDE the .lockd directory already covered by **/*.lockd* at root .gitignore:36 and by the per-initiative file. Nothing writes to /etc/, to a read-only mount, or to the caller's cwd outside the derived srd_root. .claude/worktrees/** agent trees are covered by root .gitignore:1.

edm-state update-patterns mutating tracked files inside the installed plugin directory is the intended Living-Library design -- pattern-library growth is meant to be reviewed and committed -- and its write_atomic staging path is covered by root .gitignore:16 and :37. Not a hygiene defect. Separately, score-artifacts.sh's refusal to write scores.json into the tracked fixture directory without an explicit --out (the CA-151 remediation) is present and unchanged.

Delivery-layer note, CA-130 class, not an L5 code finding: this round's L5 lens agent was launched with a tool grant set containing Read/Glob/Grep/WebFetch/WebSearch/TaskStop and no Write, Edit or Bash, so it could not create lens-L5.md or lens-L5.jsonl itself. Both artifacts were returned inline in the agent's final message for the parent to persist. Recorded so the round's tooling-notes can account for the delivery path.
